questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A city where I knew a lot would be happening so I wouldn't be lonely and would still be fun even if the classes didn't live up to my expectations.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UVA did well in informing you beforehand about what you needed to know in terms of practical things with moving to Amsterdam and are somewhat quick to respond to e-mails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Their examination system is way less streamlined than at UCPH - it took some effort to figure out the demands to pass from class to class.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got housing through UVA's housing lottery, and if I didn't get anything through them I honestly don't think I would've gone - the housing market in Amsterdam is insane. So my biggest recommendation is to absolutely sign up through the lottery - even though they say there's only housing for 50% of the applications, I barely knew any exchange students who didn't get their apartment through the lottery. The only negative thing about it is that the lottery is really late, so it's very close to the beginning of the exchange - but again, in my experience people had quite good luck. I also went in the spring semester when there are, apparently, fewer exchange students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Sign up for the lottery or start your housing hunt very early!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Was it the nicest place in the world? No. But it was a place to live in Amsterdam, so nothing to complain about.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Expect some scheduling overlaps due to their 3-block-system, but apart from that, as soon as I rescheduled my courses, I got into all of them.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: For your own sake, listen to their recommendation of doing 2-2-1 in the three blocks. I did 3-2-0, and my study pressure in the first block was really intense (it's 18 ECTS in two months including exams). I managed and passed, but if you're able to take a class in block 3, I'd probably say that's a good idea.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Just e-mail them if you have any doubts - I didn't understand what courses were available to me at first but got help from someone who could explain it quite well.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very - except from the scheduling overlap.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: What I said above - if possible: follow their guidelines in terms of study pressure.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some of them were way above my level - even though I was allowed to sign up for them. My advice would be to keep in mind that if you're an MA-student and sign up for MA-courses outside of your own field (which you'll probably have to do at UVA since their MA course catalogue is limited), do keep in mind that you'll be thrown right into a course where everyone might've already been studying that field on their MA for a year or a half, and you're expected to keep up. UVA does so many assignments and midterms apart from just the final exams, so you constantly have to hand things in (or do presentations) which means that not understanding the material from week to week isn't reaaally an option. You have to both be constantly on track + do your final paper/exam. With that being said, in my experience the profs were also really nice, understanding and helpful in terms of guiding for final paper topics when you let them know that you were a bit out of your comfort zone. And at the end of the day I did pass all of my courses, some of them just took quite some effort.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different - at UCPH I'm used to a more personal teaching style where the prof for example knows your name and you have more seminars. At UVA my experience was, in some classes at least, that you felt more anonymous + I had more lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The only thing was a water bill, but that's manageable. However, not a cost but unexpected: you might be eligible to apply for Dutch housing support for your stay!! Definitely look into that cause that's a great financial help.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out + cafes were in general less expensive than at home, but then on the other hand I usually met up with my friends out which becomes quite expensive. My advice would be to save up beforehand and apply for scholarships if you have the time, cause in my experience, once you're in Amsterdam you want to be out in the city - and there are also tons of cultural events such as concerts, plays and so on to experience which also cost money. There are good youth/student discounts for cultural events though.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really use them but seemed great.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Participate in the ESN introduction days to meet people! Even though the activities aren't that great and it's 80 euros or something - but you don't want to miss out on meeting your first friends there.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy - I think the most difficult part was to adjust to the academic culture with the block system and all the assignments and different examination system.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It's definitely easier to socialize with other exchange students, but with the locals you should just make sure to exchange contact information before the class is over if you meet someone nice and then you can ask if they wanna study together one day and take it from there. It surely is more difficult because they already have their lives and friend groups established, but it is possible, and it's really fun because they know the city better.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Sign up for the housing lottery.
Save up money before you go.
Adjust your academic expectations - you're gonna have a lot of work to hand in on your MA at UVA, and you're not gonna have time to do well in everything if you also want to enjoy the wonderful city that Amsterdam is with the lovely friends you're gonna make.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made and the experience in general of being able to move to a place where you don't know anyone or anything and establishing a really nice every day life there.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Dealing with the exams, assignments and the block system - veryyy different from UCPH with few classes and big projects for exams.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Make sure in the beginning to take any opportunity to meet people!! I went to the ESN intro days, and even though they were 82 euros and the activities were not fun, it was very important that I went cause I met my very first (and some of my best) friends there. Just power through the awkwardness of it all cause you'll meet people that's for sure.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
